name: scRNA-seq Clustering
description: Identify and characterize cell clusters from scRNA-seq
prompt:
Perform clustering on the uploaded scRNA-seq data.

Work in this order:
1. QC: filter cells/genes on counts, n_genes, and mitochondrial % (default <15-20%, adjust per tissue), flag and remove doublets with Scrublet (Python).
2. Normalize with a documented Scanpy-compatible method, select HVGs, scale, PCA; correct batch effects across samples (Harmony/scVI) and check the embedding for residual batch.
3. Run Leiden/Louvain at multiple resolutions; assess cluster stability (e.g., bootstrap/silhouette) and pick an optimal resolution.
4. Identify marker genes per cluster with the Wilcoxon rank-sum test, reporting effect sizes and BH-adjusted p-values; avoid double-dipping when interpreting.
5. Annotate clusters using {reference} markers and validate against known biology.
6. Visualize UMAP, marker expression, and report cluster proportions and distinguishing features. Set a random seed, record package versions. If an essential parameter (e.g., expected cell types or QC cutoffs) is ambiguous and would change results, ask the minimum set of blocking questions together via the interview tool; otherwise state assumptions. Save figures (PNG), marker tables (CSV), the processed .h5ad, and a methods+findings report (Markdown); summarize in chat, name the files, and note limitations.

name: Flow Cytometry Analysis
description: Gate, cluster, and quantify flow cytometry data
prompt:
Analyze the uploaded flow cytometry data (FCS files).

Work in this order:
1. Apply compensation/spillover correction and QC: remove debris/doublets (FSC-A vs FSC-H), gate on viability, check for time-based acquisition anomalies, and transform fluorescence (arcsinh/logicle).
2. Reproduce the manual gating strategy or run automated gating: {gating}.
3. Dimensionality reduction (UMAP) of marker expression.
4. Cluster with FlowSOM or PhenoGraph and annotate populations by canonical markers.
5. Quantify cell population frequencies per sample.
6. Compare populations between {comparison} using appropriate tests for the design (e.g., Mann-Whitney/t-test or mixed models for paired data) with multiple-comparison correction and effect sizes; flag batch/acquisition-day confounds. Set a random seed and record package versions. If the panel-to-marker mapping or comparison design is ambiguous and would change results, ask the minimum set of blocking questions together via the interview tool; otherwise state assumptions. Generate publication-quality dot plots and histograms (PNG), frequency tables (CSV), and a methods+findings report (Markdown); summarize in chat, name the files, and note limitations.

name: Cell-Cell Communication
prompt:
Infer cell-cell communication networks from the uploaded scRNA-seq data.

Work in this order:
1. Confirm QC, normalization, and reliable cell-type annotations first, since communication inference is only as good as the labels.
2. Identify ligand-receptor pairs between cell types and score interaction strength using a Python workflow such as LIANA or CellPhoneDB with permutation-based significance, reporting adjusted p-values.
3. Identify dominant signaling pathways.
4. Detect outgoing and incoming signals per cell type.
5. Visualize communication networks (chord diagrams, dot plots, heatmaps).
6. Compare signaling between {comparison} if multiple conditions, using differential interaction analysis and accounting for differences in cell-type abundance; flag that inferred interactions are predictions requiring spatial or functional validation. Set a random seed and record package/database versions. If conditions or the cell-type grouping are ambiguous and would change results, ask the minimum set of blocking questions together via the interview tool; otherwise state assumptions. Save figures (PNG), interaction tables (CSV), the processed object, and a methods+findings report (Markdown); summarize in chat, name files, and note limitations.

name: Cell Cycle Analysis
description: Score cell cycle phases and regress out cell cycle effects
prompt:
Perform cell cycle analysis on the uploaded scRNA-seq data.

Work in this order:
1. After normalization, score G1, S, and G2M phases using standard gene sets (e.g., Tirosh S/G2M genes), mapping to the correct species orthologs.
2. Visualize the cell cycle distribution across clusters and on UMAP.
3. Test whether cell cycle drives clustering (e.g., compare embeddings/cluster assignments before vs after, association tests).
4. Regress out or correct cell cycle effects only if it is a confounder, and report the impact; avoid removing biologically meaningful proliferation signal.
5. Compare cell cycle phase distributions between {comparison} using appropriate proportion tests with multiple-comparison correction and effect sizes.
6. Identify cell cycle-regulated genes specific to each cell type. Set a random seed and record package versions. If the comparison groups or species are ambiguous and would change results, ask the minimum set of blocking questions together via the interview tool; otherwise state assumptions. Save figures (PNG), phase/score tables (CSV), the processed .h5ad, and a methods+findings report (Markdown); summarize in chat, name files, and note limitations.

name: Perturbation / CRISPR Screen Analysis
description: Analyze Perturb-seq or CRISPR screen data
prompt:
Analyze the uploaded perturbation screen data ({screen_type}).

Work in this order:
1. QC: assess guide RNA assignment, coverage, and cell numbers per perturbation, filter low-coverage guides, run standard scRNA QC (mito %, doublets), and handle multiplets/multiple-guide cells.
2. Identify differentially expressed genes per perturbation vs non-targeting controls using a suitable model (e.g., negative-binomial/pseudobulk DE) with BH correction and reported effect sizes; avoid treating each cell as independent when pseudobulk is appropriate.
3. Score perturbation effects on gene programs/signatures.
4. Cluster perturbations by transcriptional similarity.
5. Identify genetic interactions or epistasis where the design supports it.
6. Prioritize hits for validation with explicit criteria and confidence. Set a random seed and record package versions. If the control definition or replicate structure is ambiguous and would change results, ask the minimum set of blocking questions together via the interview tool; otherwise state assumptions. Save figures (PNG), per-perturbation DE and hit tables (CSV), the processed object, and a methods+findings report (Markdown); summarize in chat, name files, and note limitations.

name: Lineage Tracing Analysis
description: Reconstruct cell lineage trees from barcoding data
prompt:
Analyze lineage tracing data from the uploaded dataset.

Work in this order:
1. Process barcode or mutation data for lineage reconstruction, with QC on barcode detection/dropout and collision filtering.
2. Build lineage trees using neighbor-joining or Bayesian/maximum-likelihood methods, reporting branch support where available.
3. Map cell types onto the lineage tree, integrating paired transcriptomic annotations if present.
4. Identify lineage-biased progenitors.
5. Quantify fate probabilities for each progenitor class with uncertainty estimates.
6. Visualize lineage trees annotated with cell types and pseudotime, and check that inferred topology is robust to barcode noise. Set a random seed and record package versions. If the barcode encoding scheme or expected lineage structure is ambiguous and would materially change results, ask the minimum set of blocking questions together via the interview tool; otherwise state assumptions. 3. Identify spatial neighborhoods and niches (e.g., neighborhood enrichment, niche clustering).

name: Metabolic Flux Analysis
prompt:
Perform metabolic flux analysis on {organism} using constraint-based modeling.

Work in this order:
1. Load or construct a genome-scale metabolic model (GEM) from a curated source and validate it (mass/charge balance, blocked reactions, sensible default biomass objective).
2. Define media conditions: {media}, setting exchange bounds explicitly and recording them.
3. Run flux balance analysis (FBA) to predict growth rate and fluxes, and sanity-check against known growth phenotypes.
4. Perform flux variability analysis (FVA) to report flux ranges and identify alternate optima.
5. Simulate single (and optionally double) gene knockouts and predict essential genes, comparing to known essentiality where available.
6. Visualize metabolic flux maps on pathway diagrams. Record solver and package versions and the model identifier/version for reproducibility. If the media composition or objective is missing/ambiguous and would materially change results, ask the minimum set of blocking questions together via the interview tool; otherwise state assumptions (e.g., default minimal media). Save flux maps and figures (PNG), flux/FVA/essentiality tables (CSV), the model file, and a concise methods+findings report (Markdown); summarize in chat, name files, and note limitations.
